Trail runners will head to Alegria, Cebu on November 28–29, 2026, for the M4M Ultra Trail Alegria 2026, a two-day trail running event organized by Bakyard.

The event features four race categories: 50K, 30K, 15K, and 8K, with courses taking runners through the mountainous landscape around Mt. Lanaya and surrounding communities.

The longest course covers more than 55 kilometers with approximately 1,900 meters of elevation gain, while the 15K and 8K routes offer shorter options through the same rugged South Cebu landscape.

The event is part of the Miles for Minds initiative, with the organizers highlighting mental-health advocacy through the race.

]]> 775 Trees Planted in Mt. Manunggal Forest Restoration Effort https://beesayatv.com/775-trees-planted-in-mt-manunggal-forest-restoration-effort/ Thu, 01 Oct 2026 23:37:01 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1866

More than 30 government agencies and partner organizations planted 775 trees and bamboo across two hectares in Barangay Sunog, Balamban, as part of a forest restoration effort in Mt. Manunggal.

The planting area is within the Central Cebu Protected Landscape, a protected area that contains important forest ecosystems and watersheds in Cebu. The species planted included indigenous forest trees, fruit trees and bamboo.

According to DENR Region 7, the activity aims to restore forest cover, support biodiversity and strengthen the ecological functions of the protected landscape.

For hikers, forest restoration in Mt. Manunggal can help protect the natural environment surrounding the trails. Healthy forests provide habitat for wildlife, help regulate water flow and support the streams and other water sources found in Cebu’s mountain areas.

Hikers visiting Mt. Manunggal and other parts of the Central Cebu Protected Landscape should stay on established trails, avoid damaging young trees and vegetation, and leave natural areas undisturbed as restoration efforts continue.

Source: DENR Region 7
Published: September 30, 2026

]]> El Niño Intensifies: What Hikers Should Prepare For https://beesayatv.com/el-nino-intensifies-what-hikers-should-prepare-for/ Wed, 30 Sep 2026 23:40:17 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1759

The Climate Change Commission (CCC) is urging government agencies, schools and communities to strengthen preparations for El Niño as dry conditions are expected to intensify across the Philippines.

The advisory follows PAGASA’s warning that the current strong El Niño could develop into a very strong event between September and December 2026 and persist through the first half of 2027.

PAGASA said El Niño generally brings warmer temperatures and below-normal rainfall, increasing the risk of prolonged dry spells, drought and pressure on water resources. Short periods of heavy rainfall may still occur because of the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones.

For hikers, prolonged dry conditions may mean hotter trails, reduced water flow in rivers and waterfalls, drier vegetation and fewer reliable natural water sources.

Hikers should carry more drinking water than usual, start early to avoid the hottest part of the day, check PAGASA and local advisories before leaving, and avoid relying on streams or springs that may normally provide water. Extra caution is also advisable in dry grasslands and forest areas where fire risk may increase.

]]> The Purpose of beesayatv’s Drone Surveys https://beesayatv.com/the-purpose-of-beesayatvs-drone-surveys/ Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:36:43 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1737

A hiking trail provides a ground-level view of a location.

It allows us to observe the condition of a route, its terrain, surrounding vegetation, and the features encountered along the way. But the view is naturally limited to where the trail passes and what can be seen from it.

Aerial observation provides another perspective.

Through Drone Surveys, beesayatv documents mountains, hillsides, rivers, access roads, and surrounding landscapes that may not be fully visible from the ground.

The objective is not simply to capture aerial footage. It is to provide additional geographic context to the places documented through fieldwork.

Understanding the Surrounding Landscape

A mountain may have several access routes approaching from different communities. A river may follow a course that is difficult to observe from a single point. A hillside may contain roads and clearings that are not visible from the hiking trail.

Aerial footage can help show how these features are situated in relation to one another.

This is particularly useful when documenting locations where the hiking route represents only a small part of the surrounding terrain.

A drone survey does not replace ground-level observation. It provides a complementary perspective that can help readers understand the broader landscape.

Giving Aerial Footage Geographic Context

A video can show a landscape without making it immediately clear where the drone was flying.

beesayatv addresses this by presenting drone footage alongside its recorded GPS flight path.

As the video plays, a moving marker follows the aircraft’s recorded position on the map.

This allows readers to relate the footage to the drone’s movement through the surveyed area.

The recorded path identifies the aircraft’s position rather than the precise location of every feature visible in the video. Nevertheless, it provides useful geographic context that ordinary aerial footage may not offer.

Documenting Different Parts of a Location

One flight cannot necessarily cover everything that is relevant to a location.

A survey may require separate flights to observe different hillsides, approach roads, river sections, or other areas of interest.

beesayatv’s Drone Surveys can now bring these recordings together, allowing readers to explore several aerial observations associated with the same location.

Each flight preserves its own recording date and flight path, including when the recordings were made during different visits.

This also allows a survey to expand as additional areas are documented.

Connecting the View From Above With the Trail Below

Aerial observation becomes more useful when it can be considered alongside ground-level fieldwork.

A drone may reveal how several roads approach a mountain, while separate trail reports document the actual conditions encountered along those routes.

Readers can move from a hiking report to the corresponding aerial observations, or from a drone survey to the connected ground-level documentation.

These are different types of fieldwork, but they can provide complementary information about the same location.

A Continuing Record of the Landscape

beesayatv Drone Surveys are intended to support continuing documentation of the places visited during fieldwork.

A location may be recorded once, revisited after several months, or surveyed again years later. Each additional flight contributes another observation made at a particular time.

These records may also provide a basis for examining visible landscape changes during future visits, provided the footage offers sufficiently comparable views.

The goal is not to produce a complete geographic survey or to replace professional mapping. It is to build an accessible collection of geographically contextualized aerial observations that complements beesayatv’s trail reports.

Explore the growing collection through the Drone Surveys directory.

]]> The Trail Itself Is the Destination https://beesayatv.com/the-trail-itself-is-the-destination/ Sun, 27 Sep 2026 12:34:13 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1680

Nature exploration is often associated with mountain summits, waterfalls, and expansive landscapes.

These places are worth documenting, but much of what makes a trail interesting exists between the starting point and the destination.

For beesayatv, the trail itself is the destination.

What Exists Along the Trail

A narrow footpath through dense vegetation may not offer a panoramic view, but it can reveal details that are easily overlooked.

Plants growing along the path, animals encountered during a hike, changes in the ground surface, and signs of human activity all provide information about the surrounding environment.

Some of these observations require stopping, looking more closely, or briefly leaving the walking pace of the hike.

They are part of the fieldwork rather than interruptions to it.

Curiosity and Documentation

Not everything encountered during a hike can be anticipated before the route is explored.

An unfamiliar plant, an unusual feature of the landscape, or a small discovery along the path may become part of the video documentation.

These encounters are recorded as they happen, without the need for narration.

The accompanying field records provide geographical context through GPS tracks, trail-surface observations, and photographs.

The video preserves what was encountered along the way, while the field data records where the hike took place.

Beyond Scenic Destinations

Not every trail leads to a waterfall, summit, or other prominent landmark.

Some connect communities, cross agricultural areas, follow rivers, or pass through narrow stretches of vegetation.

These routes are still worth documenting.

Their value as field records does not depend on whether they offer spectacular scenery or attract a large audience.

For beesayatv, documenting a trail means recording the route and observing what exists along it, not simply reaching the place at its end.

A destination may be the reason for starting a hike, but it is not the only thing worth documenting.

]]> When a Trail Still Exists but Access Doesn’t https://beesayatv.com/when-a-trail-still-exists-but-access-doesnt/ Wed, 23 Sep 2026 07:10:24 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1655

A hiking route can remain visible on a map long after access to it has changed.

That is becoming relevant in Cebu with the closure of Spartan Trail and the current discussion around possible access changes at Celestial Garden.

Spartan Trail

Spartan Trail inside the Central Cebu Protected Landscape has been officially closed until further notice while authorities investigate reported violations and conduct rehabilitation work.

The route itself has not disappeared. What changed is access.

This is an important distinction when looking at old GPX tracks, videos, and trail reports.

Celestial Garden

There is also growing discussion among hikers about possible changes to access through Celestial Garden.

At the moment, beesayatv has not found an official announcement confirming that Celestial Garden itself will be closed. Until there is one, it should be treated as an access concern rather than a confirmed closure.

Maps Do Not Show Everything

A GPX track only records where someone travelled.

It does not show land ownership, access restrictions, gates, development, or later changes in how a route is managed.

A trail can therefore remain geographically correct while becoming unusable.

This is why recent field observation, local information, and official advisories remain important even when a detailed route already exists.

For beesayatv, a trail record shows what was accessible when it was documented. It does not guarantee that the same access will remain permanent.

]]> DENR Closes Spartan Trail in Cebu Until Further Notice https://beesayatv.com/denr-closes-spartan-trail-in-cebu-until-further-notice/ Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:57:28 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1649

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has officially closed the Spartan Trail within the Central Cebu Protected Landscape until further notice.

Issued on September 21, 2026, the closure order allows authorities to investigate reported environmental violations and carry out necessary rehabilitation work in the area. Under Republic Act 9486 and Republic Act 11038, all entry, hiking, trekking, and recreational activities are strictly prohibited. Only authorized personnel involved in enforcement, monitoring, and rehabilitation are permitted to enter.

Hikers and visitors are advised to consider the Spartan Trail completely off-limits, avoid alternative entry points, and wait for an official reopening notice from authorities before planning future trips.

]]> El Niño Is Strengthening — What It Could Mean for Cebu’s Mountains and Trails https://beesayatv.com/el-nino-is-strengthening-what-it-could-mean-for-cebus-mountains-and-trails/ Sat, 19 Sep 2026 23:26:43 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?p=1644

A strong El Niño is currently established across the tropical Pacific and is projected to intensify further over the coming months.

According to PAGASA and the World Meteorological Organization, moderate to strong conditions are expected to reach very strong intensity by late 2026, with a high likelihood of persisting into early 2027.

For Cebu and the broader Philippines, this climate event typically triggers below-normal rainfall, dry spells, and potential drought, though localized rain and Habagat showers remain possible.

Hikers and local residents in Cebu’s uplands should anticipate hotter and drier trail conditions, drying vegetation, and reduced water levels in mountain streams as the dry conditions progress.
